steps.text: On Thursday: Remove the turkey from the brine, discard the brine, and pat the turkey thoroughly dry with paper towels.
Let the turkey sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Mash 6 tablespoons softened butter with 3 minced garlic cloves and 1 teaspoon black pepper; loosen the skin over the breast and thighs and push 4 sage sprigs and 2 rosemary sprigs under the skin.

Rub the herb butter all over the outside of the bird; drizzle 2 tablespoons olive oil over the skin; stuff the cavity with 3 halved garlic cloves, 1 halved lemon, 1 quartered onion, and 4 thyme sprigs.

Scatter 3 celery stalks and 2 carrots (cut into large pieces) in the bottom of a large roasting pan; set the turkey breast-side up on a roasting rack over the vegetables and pour 2 cups chicken broth into the pan.
Roast the turkey at 325°F for about 2¾ hours; baste with pan drippings every 45 minutes.
Raise the oven to 350°F and put in the Sage and Onion Stuffing and Green Bean Casserole.
Keep roasting the turkey at 350°F for about 25 more minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F.
Transfer the turkey to a carving board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 20–30 minutes before carving; reserve the pan drippings for the gravy.
Carve the turkey and arrange on a large platter.
Serve the Herb-Roasted Whole Turkey with the Pan Gravy, Sage and Onion Stuffing, Mashed Potatoes, Cranberry-Orange Sauce, Green Bean Casserole and Sweet Potato Casserole.

On Thursday: pour the turkey drippings from the roasting pan into a fat separator or large measuring cup; skim off and reserve ½ cup fat (supplement with 4 tablespoons butter if needed), leaving the dark juices behind.
Set the roasting pan over two burners on medium-high; add the reserved fat and whisk in ½ cup all-purpose flour, scraping up all the browned bits, and cook 2 minutes until the roux smells nutty.
Gradually whisk in the stock and the reserved pan juices; bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer and cook 8–10 minutes, whisking often, until the gravy is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Strip the leaves from 2 thyme sprigs.
Stir the thyme leaves in; season with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and ½ teaspoon black pepper, then pour the gravy into a warm gravy boat.
On Thursday: The stuffing is in at 350°F, covered. Bake 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes more until the top is golden and crisp.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Let the stuffing rest 5 minutes.

On Thursday: peel 5 pounds russet potatoes and cut into 2-inch chunks; put them in a large pot (at least 8-quart), cover with cold salted water by 2 inches, and leave the pot on the stove, off, until it's time to cook.
Turn the burner on under the pot of potatoes and bring to a boil over high heat.
Boil the potatoes over medium-high heat for 18–20 minutes until completely tender when pierced with a fork; drain well and return to the pot.
Warm 1 cup whole milk and ½ cup heavy cream together in a small saucepan or microwave until steaming; mash the drained potatoes with 10 tablespoons butter until smooth.
Stir in the warm milk-cream mixture gradually until the potatoes reach your preferred consistency; season with 2 teaspoons kosher salt and ¼ teaspoon white pepper.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Transfer the potatoes to a warm serving bowl and garnish with 2 tablespoons thinly sliced fresh chives, if using.
On Thursday: The green bean casserole is in at 350°F, covered. Bake 25 minutes.
Uncover, scatter 6 ounces fried onions evenly over the top, and bake uncovered 10 minutes more until the onions are golden and crisp.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
On Thursday: Put the sweet potato casserole in the oven.
The sweet potato casserole is in at 350°F, covered. Bake 20 minutes.
Uncover and bake 10 minutes more until the streusel is golden and the filling is hot — if using marshmallows, broil 1–2 minutes at the very end until toasted.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
On Thursday: whip 1 cup heavy cream to soft peaks and serve alongside the chilled pie, if using.
Finely chop the 1½ lb cremini mushrooms, mince the 4 shallots and 6 garlic cloves, and strip 2 tablespoons thyme leaves and chop 1 tablespoon rosemary.

Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high; cook the shallots and garlic 3 minutes, then add the mushrooms, thyme, and rosemary and cook 12–15 minutes, stirring often, until completely dry.

Pour in ¼ cup dry sherry, cook 2 minutes until evaporated, then stir in ½ cup fresh breadcrumbs, ½ cup toasted walnuts, and 2 oz grated vegetarian Parmesan-style cheese; season with ½ teaspoon kosher salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper and let cool.
Open both 7 oz jars of pre-made duxelles and transfer to a bowl; stir in ½ cup toasted walnuts, ½ cup fresh breadcrumbs, and 2 oz grated vegetarian Parmesan-style cheese.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high; sear the 4 portobello caps gill-side down 3 minutes per side, season with ½ teaspoon salt, then cool on a rack.
Wilt the 4 oz baby spinach in the same skillet over medium heat, 2 minutes; transfer to a colander and press out all liquid, then chop roughly.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a large rimmed sheet pan with parchment.
Lay one puff pastry sheet on a lightly floured surface; brush the center third with 1½ tablespoons Dijon mustard.
Spread half the duxelles mixture over the mustard zone, top with the spinach and then 2 seared portobello caps; repeat for the second pastry sheet with the remaining filling and caps.
Fold and roll each pastry around its filling, seam-side down on the sheet pan; brush all over with beaten egg and score the tops lightly.
Bake on the sheet pan at 425°F for 25–30 minutes until deep golden brown; rest 5 minutes before slicing into portions.
Slice each Wellington into portions.
Serve the Mushroom Wellington with the Mushroom Gravy, Herb Stuffing, Mashed Potatoes, Balsamic Roasted Brussels Sprouts, Cranberry-Orange Sauce and Baked Mac and Cheese.
Thinly slice 1 lb cremini mushrooms, mince 3 shallots and 4 garlic cloves.
Melt 4 tablespoons butter in a 4-quart saucepan over medium-high; add the 3 shallots and 4 cloves minced garlic and cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add the 1 lb sliced mushrooms and cook 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and their liquid has evaporated.
Sprinkle ⅓ cup flour over the mushrooms and stir 1–2 minutes until the raw flour smell is gone.
Pour in ¼ cup dry sherry and cook 1 minute, then gradually whisk in 4 cups vegetable broth until smooth.
Add 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 tablespoon thyme leaves, ¾ teaspoon salt, and ¼ teaspoon pepper; simmer over medium-low 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened to gravy consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning; keep warm over the lowest heat, stirring occasionally, until ready to serve.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
On Thursday: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Bake the stuffing covered at 375°F for 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 20–25 minutes more until the top is golden and crisp.
Cover the Herb Stuffing with foil to keep it warm while the oven heats for the next dish.
Return the Herb Stuffing, uncovered, to the 425°F oven for 10 minutes, until hot again.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Thinly slice 2 tbsp fresh chives; keep it covered in a small container in the fridge until serving.

Peel and cut 5 lb russet potatoes into 2-inch chunks; put them in a large pot with the 4 peeled garlic cloves, cover with cold salted water, and leave the pot on the stove, off, until it's time to cook.
Turn the burner on under the pot of potatoes.
Bring the pot to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a vigorous simmer and cook 18–20 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender when pierced.
Warm 1 cup whole milk in a small saucepan over low heat until steaming; keep warm.
Drain the potatoes and garlic, return to the pot, and let steam dry 2 minutes over low heat.
Mash the potatoes and garlic with 8 tablespoons butter until smooth, then stir in the warm milk, ½ cup sour cream, 1½ teaspoons salt, and ¼ teaspoon white pepper.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Transfer the potatoes to a serving bowl and garnish with the chives you sliced this morning.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Trim and halve 3 lb Brussels sprouts.
Whisk together ¼ cup olive oil, 3 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, 1½ tablespoons honey, 4 minced garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon salt, and ½ teaspoon pepper in a large bowl.
Toss the Brussels sprouts in the balsamic mixture and spread cut-side down in a single layer across two large rimmed sheet pans.
Roast at 425°F for 22–25 minutes, rotating the pans halfway through, until the sprouts are deeply caramelized and tender.
Cover the Balsamic Roasted Brussels Sprouts with foil to keep them warm.
Return the Balsamic Roasted Brussels Sprouts, uncovered, to the 425°F oven for 10 minutes, until hot again.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Transfer the Brussels sprouts to a serving platter, scatter with ¼ cup dried cranberries, and top with 3 tablespoons toasted pine nuts if using.
On Thursday: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
On Thursday: Toss 1 cup panko breadcrumbs with 2 tablespoons melted butter and the remaining 4 oz sharp cheddar; scatter evenly over the cold mac and cheese.
Bake uncovered at 375°F for 45–50 minutes until the crumb topping is deep golden and the edges are bubbling.
Cover the Baked Mac and Cheese with foil to keep it warm.
Return the Baked Mac and Cheese, uncovered, to the 425°F oven for 10 minutes, until hot again.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Let the mac and cheese rest 5 minutes.
On Thursday: Slice the Apple Pie and serve.
